reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that modern football increasingly relies on data-driven approaches to evaluate and improve performance. Curve similarity captures how closely a player's blocking motion aligns with optimal patterns, serving as a proxy for technical proficiency. Expected depth models the anticipated vertical advancement of a lineman at a critical moment—3.5 seconds post-snap—using contextual features like down, distance, and field position. This allows for a probabilistic assessment of whether a player is performing above or below expected norms. Development trajectory extends these concepts temporally, modeling how individual skills evolve over time. These primitives form a coherent mathematical framework for evaluating not just current performance but also potential for growth, integrating both static and dynamic aspects of player behavior. Failure modes include misalignment between model assumptions and real-world variability, particularly in high-pressure situations or when new techniques emerge. Dualities arise between short-term execution (depth) and long-term potential (trajectory), suggesting that optimizing one may require trade-offs with the other.
